lessonRef.unitTitle: Senior Capstone: Independent Research and Defense
lessonRef.title: Assessment preparation: routine writing over extended time frames

rubric.description: The learner states the method they chose and the known weakness of that method.
Every claim is traceable to a source the learner assessed for strengths and limitations relative to this task.
The learner reports what the evidence does not establish and what would overturn the claim.

scoringAuthority.scoringGuidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid readings when the evidence supports them. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

acceptableAnswerCriteria.text: The learner states the method they chose and the known weakness of that method. Every claim is traceable to a source the learner assessed for strengths and limitations relative to this task. The learner reports what the evidence does not establish and what would overturn the claim. I directly answer the question about routine writing over extended time frames and complete the named deliverable. I use three precise citations, a limitation, and a defensible qualification from “Reading Lab 177: routine writing over extended time frames” and identify where the evidence appears. I explain how the evidence supports my thinking, then check clarity, accuracy, and completion before submitting. I address a meaningful complication, alternative interpretation, counterclaim, or limitation when the evidence calls for one. I qualify the conclusion so it does not claim more certainty or scope than the delivered source can support. Evidence must be traceable to the delivered Academy-original text “Reading Lab 177: routine writing over extended time frames” by paragraph number or another precise location rather than a general impression. Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require self-directed application on at least two separate occasions with no supplied method, including one piece defended against prepared objections from a reader outside the household when the family chooses.

masteryCriteria.rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require self-directed application on at least two separate occasions with no supplied method, including one piece defended against prepared objections from a reader outside the household when the family chooses.

authorshipPolicy: The learner writes every assessed response. The tutor may explain, question, critique, or suggest a revision direction.
The tutor must not draft, rewrite, or supply sentences for an assessed response, and must not complete a graded task on the learner's behalf.
Tutor assistance is logged as guided evidence; unaided work is logged as independent evidence. Mastery requires independent evidence.
Fixed-form assessment items keep their answer key adult-only; the key is never surfaced in a learner-facing surface.
doNotUse: Do not write, dictate, outline, or complete the learner's response.
This rubric describes what to look for, not a single required answer — accept any response that meets the criteria.
